Acknowledgement.description: Response to an accepted command that does its work asynchronously.
Acknowledgement.title: Acknowledgement

AnalyzerTool.description:
Tools that may produce a finding. Semgrep is CUT for the seven-day build
(P1-2) and is absent deliberately — adding it back is a scope decision.
AnalyzerTool.title: AnalyzerTool

ArtifactRef.description:
Pointer to an artifact in the encrypted store.

The URI is opaque and is never a browser-resolvable link. The UI exchanges it for
a signed, short-lived URL through the evidence endpoints — raw archives and
unsanitized logs never reach the browser directly
(`docs/03-technical/21-api-specification.md`, API rules).
ArtifactRef.title: ArtifactRef

AuthorizationRecord.description:
An operator's declaration of authority over a target repository.

Immutable once written. Revocation is a new field, not an edit — the audit trail
in the evidence bundle has to show that authority existed at the moment each
stage ran.

evidence_ref.description: Artifact pointer to the signed authorization document, if one exists.
evidence_ref.title: Evidence Ref

expires_at.description: Hard expiry. A stage starting after this instant is refused.
expires_at.title: Expires At

granted_by.description: Named human accountable for the claim.
granted_by.title: Granted By

repository_ref.description: Repository the authority covers: URL or uploaded archive name.
repository_ref.title: Repository Ref

snapshot_sha256.description: Bound snapshot digest. Once set, the authorization covers this snapshot and no other.
snapshot_sha256.title: Snapshot Sha256

statement.description: Operator's declaration of authority and scope. Reproduced verbatim in the evidence bundle.
statement.title: Statement

AuthorizationRecord.title: AuthorizationRecord

AuthorizationRequest.description:
Operator input. The server owns ids and timestamps; the client cannot set
`granted_at`, so an expired authority cannot be back-dated into validity.

valid_for_minutes.description: Lifetime of the authority, capped at 24 hours.
valid_for_minutes.title: Valid For Minutes

AuthorizationRequest.title: AuthorizationRequest

BaselineReport.description: The denominator for 'regression preserved' (P0-5). Real counts or nothing.

passed.description: The D3 gate signal, derived from the recorded counts: configure and build succeeded, at least one test ran, and none failed. Emitted alongside the BASELINE_PASSED / BASELINE_FAILED event types. It is an outcome, not a mission state.
passed.title: Passed

BaselineReport.title: BaselineReport

confirm.description: Cancellation tears down sandboxes and stops the run; it is always confirmed explicitly.
confirm.title: Confirm

CandidateVerdict.description: One candidate's outcome, for the side-by-side view.

summary.description: One-line reason, e.g. 'regression suite: 2 of 14 failed'.
summary.title: Summary

CandidateVerdict.title: CandidateVerdict

detail.description: Failure class only. Never a DSN, credential, or driver message that could carry one.
detail.title: Detail

DiscoveryMethod.description:
How a finding came to exist. Required on every finding; no default.

`FUZZING_CAMPAIGN` is the strongest claim and the only one that supports "our
fuzzer discovered it". The other two are honest and weaker: the seven-day plan
already names direct harnessing as the *starting* position rather than the
fallback, and #83 adds reproducer replay under that.
DiscoveryMethod.title: DiscoveryMethod

ErrorCode.description:
The error vocabulary from `docs/03-technical/21-api-specification.md`, plus
the transport-level codes the API cannot avoid emitting.

`GPU_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` is retained even though rented GPU is CUT (D-015): the local
model host is leased and torn down the same way, and dropping the code would make
the evidence bundles of a future run unreadable by an older client.
ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

details.description: Structured, sanitized context for the UI: allowed transitions, field errors, the issue tracking an unimplemented stub.
details.title: Details

message.description: User-safe explanation. Never contains secrets, credentials, raw target output, or unsanitized source.
message.title: Message

ErrorEnvelope.description: The single error shape every non-2xx response uses.

trace_id.description: Correlates this failure with the server logs and the mission event stream. Also returned as the X-Trace-Id header.
trace_id.title: Trace Id

ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope

EventType.description: Every event the UI can receive. Adding a member is a contract change.
EventType.title: EventType

gates_not_run.description: Gates that did not run, disclosed rather than omitted.
gates_not_run.title: Gates Not Run

isolation_mode.description: How the target was contained. Required, with no default (D-049): the previous default claimed ROOTLESS_CONTAINER, which is the stronger of the two, so a bundle assembled by code that forgot the field overclaimed the isolation posture. A subprocess jail (#81) is weaker and is reported as what it is.

patches.description: Every candidate the mission produced, accepted and rejected alike. The rejected one is the differentiator, not an embarrassment.
patches.title: Patches

recommended_patch_id.description: The one diff we stand behind. Derived and validated, not free-form: it must name a patch in `patches` whose verification verdict is VERIFIED, and when exactly one candidate verified it must be that one. A bundle showing two verified patches without naming one invites a judge to pick the wrong one and ask why we shipped it.
recommended_patch_id.title: Recommended Patch Id

substitutions.description: Every fallback path used in this run. Empty means the primary path ran throughout — a claim the pipeline has to earn, not assume.
substitutions.title: Substitutions

verdict_summary.description: The mission verdict and the per-candidate breakdown it was derived from.

verifications.description: One record per candidate, each with its own gate matrix.
verifications.title: Verifications

EvidenceSource.description:
Whether a gate result came from running a tool or from a stored artifact.

A gate may only PASS on `TOOL_EXECUTION`. A replayed artifact can be recorded and
displayed; it cannot pass a gate.
EvidenceSource.title: EvidenceSource

include_artifacts.description: Bundle raw artifacts alongside the report. Never includes the target's source archive.
include_artifacts.title: Include Artifacts

code_slice.description: The relevant source region only. Never the whole repository.
code_slice.title: Code Slice

sanitizer_report.description: Sanitized sanitizer output: stack frames and the failure kind. Absolute paths and environment values are stripped before it reaches here.
sanitizer_report.title: Sanitizer Report

discovery_method.description: How this finding came to exist. Required, with no default: only FUZZING_CAMPAIGN supports the claim 'our fuzzer discovered it'. A replayed reproducer (#83) is honest and weaker, and has to say so.

replay_source.description: Artifact pointer to the recorded reproducer. Required when discovery_method is REPLAYED_REPRODUCER, and forbidden otherwise.
replay_source.title: Replay Source

reproducible.description: True only when a minimized input replayed the failure from a clean build. Not a guess.
reproducible.title: Reproducible

FuzzingMode.description: Whether a fuzzing campaign actually ran (#83).
FuzzingMode.title: FuzzingMode

mode.description: Whether a campaign actually ran. Required, no default — a replayed corpus (#83) cannot be reported as a live campaign.

replay_source.description: Artifact pointer to the recorded corpus. Required when mode is REPLAYED_CORPUS, forbidden otherwise.
replay_source.title: Replay Source

GateMatrix.description: The complete evidence basis for a verdict. Nothing else is consulted.
GateMatrix.title: GateMatrix

GateResult.description:
One deterministic gate's outcome, with the tool that produced it.

A gate may only `PASS` on the strength of a tool that actually ran. Replayed
artifacts are recordable — the fallbacks in #82 and #83 need them — but a replayed
artifact cannot pass a gate, and a `PASS` with no named tool cannot be constructed.
That is what stops a mission whose fuzzer never ran from claiming the renewed-fuzz
gate as evidence.

detail.description: User-safe summary. Never raw target output, never secrets.
detail.title: Detail

evidence_ref.description: Opaque artifact pointer (artifact://...). Resolved through a signed short-lived link, never returned inline.
evidence_ref.title: Evidence Ref

evidence_source.description: Where this result came from. Required, with no default (D-049): a default here is a claim the system makes on the caller's behalf when they say nothing, and the old default said 'a tool ran'. Code populating a gate from a stored artifact that forgot this field used to PASS the gate. A REPLAYED_ARTIFACT result may be recorded and displayed; it may not be PASS, and a NOT_RUN result may not claim TOOL_EXECUTION.

tool.description: Tool that produced this result, e.g. 'ctest 3.28.3'. Empty when NOT_RUN.
tool.title: Tool

GateResult.title: GateResult

GateStatus.description: Outcome of one deterministic gate. There is no `LIKELY` and no score.
GateStatus.title: GateStatus

InferenceMode.description:
Whether a model response was generated live or replayed from a transcript.

Required on every `ModelProvenance`; no default, by the same reasoning as
`DiscoveryMethod` and `FuzzingMode` (D-049). D-015 cut the rented GPU, so the D5
gate rests on a quantized CPU-served model and a replay-mode gateway is the
approved fallback. Serving a captured response is legitimate; letting silence
claim it was generated live is not.
InferenceMode.title: InferenceMode

IsolationMode.description:
How the target was contained (#81, #15).

`SUBPROCESS_JAIL` is materially weaker than either container mode and it is an
acceptable D3 fallback; it must never be reported as a container path.

`CONTAINER_NO_NETWORK` [Δ #15] is D-024's accepted substitute for rootless
isolation: a standard (rootful-daemon) container with `--network none`, a fixed
non-root uid, every capability dropped, `no-new-privileges`, and a read-only root
filesystem — every property in `docs/09-company/08-security-review.md` §6.2
*except* the user-namespace remapping true rootless would add. D-024 condition 8
is binding: a run in this mode is never reported as `ROOTLESS_CONTAINER`, because
that would claim the one property (`--network none` aside) it does not deliver —
protection against a container-runtime escape reaching host root.

`ROOTLESS_CONTAINER` is kept for a genuine rootless Podman/Docker run, should one
ever land; nothing in this codebase produces it today.
IsolationMode.title: IsolationMode

text.description: Sanitized, user-safe line. Never raw target output and never anything carrying a credential.
text.title: Text

MissionCounts.description: Summary counters. Every one is a real count from the evidence database.
MissionCounts.title: MissionCounts

idempotency_key.description: Replaying a create with the same key returns the same mission rather than creating a second one.
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

repository_ref.description: Authorized repository URL or the name of an uploaded archive. Never a public target chosen at scan time.
repository_ref.title: Repository Ref

allowed_transitions.description: What the operator controls may legally do next. The UI disables its buttons from this rather than duplicating the state machine.
allowed_transitions.title: Allowed Transitions

authorization.description: The record itself. Absent means nothing may run.

verdict.description: The mission verdict, derived from the set of per-candidate verdicts. Never displayed without `verdict_summary` beside it.

verdict_summary.description: Per-candidate breakdown. A mission runs N candidates through the identical pipeline — the demo runs two, one Verified and one Rejected — and the rejection is the differentiator, so it travels with the mission verdict rather than being reduced away.

MissionEvent.description: One immutable mission event. Append-only; never edited after emission.

evidence_refs.description: Opaque artifact pointers; resolved through the evidence endpoints, never linked directly.
evidence_refs.title: Evidence Refs

message.description: User-safe line for the event rail. Sanitized at the source.
message.title: Message

metrics.description: Real measured telemetry only. No decorative values — a metric the pipeline cannot measure is absent, not zero.
metrics.title: Metrics

payload.description: Typed, discriminated on `kind`. Everything the UI renders comes from here.
payload.title: Payload

sequence.description: Gap-free per-mission ordinal. Also the SSE `id:` field, so a reconnecting client can detect and replay a gap.
sequence.title: Sequence

stage.description: Workflow stage in progress, when one applies.

trace_id.description: Correlates this event with the request and the server logs.
trace_id.title: Trace Id

MissionEvent.title: MissionEvent

reproducer_replay_attempts.description: How many times a minimized input must replay from a clean build before `reproducible` is set.
reproducer_replay_attempts.title: Reproducer Replay Attempts

MissionPosture.description:
What the Core displays. Derived from `MissionState`, never set directly.

`CANCELLED` extends the list in `docs/02-design/00-ui-design-direction.md`, which
names eight postures and has no home for a deliberately-cancelled mission. Folding
it into `FAILED` would show a red alert ring on the most visible element in the
product for an operator action that worked exactly as intended.
MissionPosture.title: MissionPosture

MissionProgress.description: What the Core renders. Derived server-side so two clients never disagree.
MissionProgress.title: MissionProgress

MissionStage.description:
The nine workflow steps: authorize → ingest → baseline → analyze →
stress-test → correlate → patch → verify → export evidence.

Note the ordering of `ANALYZE`/`STRESS_TEST`/`CORRELATE`. The workflow sentence
repeated across the pack reads "analyze → correlate → stress-test"; the
architecture document's state machine reads `TRIAGE → STRESS_TEST → CORRELATE`.
The state machine ordering is used, because correlation joins static and dynamic
evidence and therefore cannot precede the dynamic run that produces it.
MissionStage.title: MissionStage

MissionState.description:
Persistent mission state machine.

Extends the sequence in `docs/03-technical/16-system-architecture-document.md`
§"Mission state machine" with the states the nine-step demo needs and the
document only implies:

* `AUTHORIZED` — the authorization record exists and is active. Nothing may run
  before this state; see `contracts.state_machine`.
* `EXPORTING`  — evidence bundle being written. The mission is not `VERIFIED`
  until the evidence exists (P0-12).
* `PAUSED` / `CANCELLING` — operator controls in the API specification that the
  document's state list omitted.
MissionState.title: MissionState

authorized.description: True only when an unrevoked, unexpired authorization record exists. Derived from the record, never set directly.
authorized.title: Authorized

MissionVerdictPayload.description:
The mission verdict and every candidate verdict behind it.

Emitted once, when the mission reaches a terminal verdict state. The Command
Center renders the candidates side by side from this — the `Verified` and the
`Rejected` together — rather than reducing them to one badge.
MissionVerdictPayload.title: MissionVerdictPayload

MissionVerdictSummary.description:
The mission verdict, and every candidate verdict it was derived from.

The demo's whole point is showing a `Verified` beside a `Rejected`. A single
mission-level verdict that hid the rejection would remove the differentiator, so
the breakdown travels with the verdict everywhere it is displayed.
MissionVerdictSummary.title: MissionVerdictSummary

ModelProvenance.description:
Where a model-generated candidate came from, and how sure the model claimed
to be.

`confidence` is recordable and displayable. It is not an input to any gate, any
verdict, or any routing decision — see the module docstring of
`contracts.verdict`. If you find yourself wanting to branch on it, that is the
bug the rule exists to prevent.

captured_at.description: When the replayed transcript was originally generated.
captured_at.title: Captured At

confidence.description: DISPLAY ONLY. The model's self-reported confidence. Cannot influence a verdict, a gate, or an escalation; recorded so the evidence bundle shows what the model claimed alongside what the tools proved.
confidence.title: Confidence

inference_mode.description: LIVE_INFERENCE or REPLAYED_TRANSCRIPT. Required, no default: a default here would be the system making a provenance claim on the caller's behalf when they said nothing, and every such default should point at the weaker claim or not exist. Whatever renders provenance reads this.

replayed_from_transcript.description: Set when this response was replayed from a captured transcript rather than generated live. Whatever renders provenance must say 'replayed'.
replayed_from_transcript.title: Replayed From Transcript

served_from.description: Host serving the model. Always local or private — validated at startup by contracts.checks.check_model_endpoints.
served_from.title: Served From

transcript_sha256.description: Digest of the replayed transcript, so the claim is checkable.
transcript_sha256.title: Transcript Sha256

ModelProvenance.title: ModelProvenance

diff.description: Unified diff, sanitized, rendered in the UI.
diff.title: Diff

model.description: Present only when provenance is MODEL_GENERATED.

provenance.description: MODEL_GENERATED or OPERATOR_SUPPLIED. Never inflated: an operator-written candidate is labelled as one in the UI and the report.

rationale.description: The model's stated reasoning. Displayed separately from evidence and never treated as evidence.
rationale.title: Rationale

PatchPolicy.description: The limits that make a rejection demonstrable as well as safe (P0-9).

allowed_paths.description: Glob allowlist. A candidate touching anything else is rejected before it is ever built.
allowed_paths.title: Allowed Paths

PatchPolicy.title: PatchPolicy

PatchProvenance.description:
Where a candidate came from. Never inflated: an operator-authored candidate
is labelled as one in the UI and in the evidence bundle (P0 cut §3, D-008).
PatchProvenance.title: PatchProvenance

PreflightReport.description: Validates authorization, commands, adapter and limits before anything runs.

blocking_codes.description: Error codes that must clear before the mission may start.
blocking_codes.title: Blocking Codes

PreflightReport.title: PreflightReport

ResourceUsage.description:
Measured, never estimated. Displayed in the Core's resource rail and written
into the evidence bundle (P0-14).

gpu_seconds.description: Zero for the seven-day build: rented GPU is cut (D-015). The field stays so an evidence bundle keeps one shape across versions.
gpu_seconds.title: Gpu Seconds

SandboxPolicy.description: Resource ceilings and the isolation posture for the target sandbox (P0-2).

network.description: Egress is denied. There is no other permitted value — the type is the enforcement.
network.title: Network

runtime.description: Container runtime, or the subprocess-jail fallback (#81). `docker` is D-024's accepted substitute for rootless Podman — a standard rootful-daemon container with `--network none`, never reported as `podman`'s stronger isolation claim. The subprocess-jail fallback is weaker isolation still and is reported as such everywhere it is used — it is not a silent substitution.
runtime.title: Runtime

SandboxPolicy.title: SandboxPolicy

isolation_mode.description: Required, no default. A subprocess jail (#81) is a legitimate D3 fallback and materially weaker than a rootless container; it cannot be reported as one.

network.description: Reported, and only ever this value.
network.title: Network

immutable.description: Snapshots are write-once. The field exists so the evidence bundle states the property rather than implying it.
immutable.title: Immutable

SnapshotRequest.description:
Ingest an immutable snapshot of the authorized repository (P0-1).

The digest is supplied by the caller and re-computed server-side; a mismatch is
a hard failure, so a swapped archive cannot inherit an existing authorization.

archive_ref.description: Pointer to the uploaded archive when source='upload'.
archive_ref.title: Archive Ref

SnapshotRequest.title: SnapshotRequest

percent_complete.description: Null when the stage genuinely cannot report progress. The UI shows an indeterminate indicator rather than inventing a number.
percent_complete.title: Percent Complete

confirm_authorized.description: Explicit operator confirmation. Typed as a literal so an accidental `false` is a validation error rather than a silent no-op.
confirm_authorized.title: Confirm Authorized

Substitution.description:
One fallback path that was used instead of the primary one.

The CEO approved fallbacks for D1–D7 (#81, #82, #83). Using one is legitimate;
letting a reader infer it from a missing section is not. Every substitution is
declared here, printed in the report, and shown in the UI.

artifact_ref.description: The recorded artifact the substitution drew on, where one exists.
artifact_ref.title: Artifact Ref

reason.description: Why the primary path was not used. Stated plainly.
reason.title: Reason

Substitution.title: Substitution

SubstitutionKind.description:
The fallback paths that exist. Any that was used is disclosed in the evidence
bundle rather than inferred by a reader from a missing section.
SubstitutionKind.title: SubstitutionKind

confirm.description: Operator-confirmed emergency teardown. Destructive and deliberate; there is no unconfirmed form.
confirm.title: Confirm

Verdict.description: The only three outcomes a verification run can produce (P0-11).
Verdict.title: Verdict

VerificationRecord.description:
A verdict and the deterministic gates that produced it.

The validator re-runs `derive_verdict` over the gates and rejects any record
whose verdict does not follow from them. This is the structural form of "a patch
is never accepted on model confidence alone": there is no way to construct,
persist, or serialize a `VERIFIED` record over a failing regression gate.

worktree_sha256.description: Digest of the clean worktree the verification ran in.
worktree_sha256.title: Worktree Sha256

VerificationRecord.title: VerificationRecord

info.description:
Control API for Brahmadatta AI — an authorized, defensive Cyber-Reasoning System.

**Contract status.** Frozen at D1 (issues #6, #9). Every endpoint except
`GET /system/health` returns `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` with the standard error envelope;
the request and response schemas are final and are what the Command Center types
against.

**Rules the schemas enforce rather than describe.**

* A verdict is derived only from the deterministic gate matrix. Model confidence is
  recorded on `ModelProvenance` for display and cannot reach the derivation; a
  `VerificationRecord` whose verdict does not follow from its gates cannot be
  serialized.
* No mission stage runs without an active authorization record.
* Sandbox network policy is typed `"deny"` and has no other permitted value.
* No inference endpoint may address a hosted third party; that is validated at
  startup by a Django system check.

**Errors.** Every non-2xx response is an `ErrorEnvelope` carrying a code from the
frozen vocabulary and the request's trace id, which is also returned as `X-Trace-Id`.
info.title: Brahmadatta AI Control API

get.description:
Server-sent events over ASGI, backed by the persisted `MissionEvent` log.

Every ORM read runs through `sync_to_async` in `api.sse`, once per call — this
view never holds an `asgiref` thread-pool thread between reads (CTO-C1). The
per-mission concurrent-stream cap is enforced with `sse.acquire_slot` *before*
`StreamingHttpResponse` is constructed, so a caller over the limit gets a real
`429` rather than a stream that opens and immediately closes; `sse.release_slot`
runs from the generator's `finally`, so a client disconnect (the ASGI handler
closing this generator) frees the slot regardless of which frame it happened on.

`Last-Event-ID` (sent automatically by a reconnecting `EventSource`) or an
explicit `?since_sequence=` resumes from a cursor and replays every missed event
in order before the stream goes live — see `sse.event_frames`.

200.description: Ordered mission event stream. Each frame is `id: <sequence>`, `event: <MissionEvent.type>`, `data: <MissionEvent as JSON>`. Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`, or replay through `/missions/{mission_id}/events/replay`.

get.description: Gap recovery for the SSE stream. `sequence` is gap-free per mission, so a client that sees a jump replays from its last known value. Reads the same persisted `MissionEvent` log the stream tails, through the same schema conversion (`api.sse.to_schema`) — there is one definition of what an event looks like, not one for the live path and a second for gap recovery.
get.summary: Replay ordered events from a sequence number
